title: Ephemeral control-plane siphon & swap playbook for private VPC upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Provide an automated, low-risk method to introduce a new control-plane version into customer VPCs by creating ephemeral control-plane instances, siphoning a small fraction of traffic for verification, executing a fast swap if health gates pass, and enabling deterministic rollback paths. This reduces blast radius for private upgrades while using Terraform/IaC primitives and observability hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module can create ephemeral control-plane stacks in a customer VPC without mutating production control-plane resources
Automated siphon route diverts 2% of API traffic to ephemeral control plane and returns canonical responses within SLA budget
Health gate checks (API contract, CRD symlinks, DB migrations dry-run) pass in staging within 15 minutes
Rollback completes within configured 5 minutes and leaves system in pre-upgrade state with zero loss of persisted state
Playbook runs end-to-end in a simulated tenant environment and produces an audit log that maps to our console trace format
implementation_notes: Create terraform/private_controlplane_ephemeral module to provision ephemeral control-plane (control-plane-ephemeral) using same operator chart but isolated k8s namespace and ephemeral metadata tags
Module exposes variables: upstream_controlplane_endpoint, siphon_ratio, preflight_checks (list), canary_duration_minutes, rollback_timeout_minutes
Preflight tasks implemented as k8s Jobs + dry-run schema validation against CRDs and operator image compatibility matrix
Traffic siphoning implemented with ingress split: create SiphonRoute CRD pointing to ephemeral endpoints and configure canary weights via module
Health gates wired into telemetry: synthetic smoke tests (token auth, model list, inference path), KV cache warmup, and end-to-end latency percentile checks
Ensure operator supports concurrent control-plane variants via feature-flag shim to prevent CRD name collisions
Stateful migrations are executed as reversible dry-run steps recorded in Confluence runbook with automatic snapshot triggers
steps: 1) Create ephemeral control-plane via terraform module in customer sandbox VPC using same IAM roles but isolated k8s cluster/namespace
2) Run preflight suite (CRD validation, schema diff, operator smoke) in dry-run mode and collect results
3) If preflight passes, update ingress to create SiphonRoute at 2% traffic with automatic canary weight ramping over 30 minutes
4) Monitor health gates: api-contract-check, model-load-success, latency-p50/p95, and error-rate. Fail fast on regressions beyond thresholds
5) If continuous health for canary_duration_minutes, perform controlled swap by updating DNS/ingress weights to 100% and decommission upstream endpoints
6) Post-swap reconciliation: run migration-finalize steps and archive audit artifacts; run synthetic test suite across 100 tenant tokens
7) If at any point threshold breached, invoke rollback task: revert ingress weight to prior control-plane and decommission ephemeral stack, capture incident diagnostics
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: CRD and operator version mismatch causing resource corruption. Mitigation: run CRD-only dry-run and ensure operator backward compatibility shim. Fail upgrade if CRD drift > 0%

Risk: Siphon path sees different caching behavior and returns divergent results. Mitigation: synthetic tests include cache-warm paths and content-bisection utilities to compare outputs deterministically
Risk: Terraform drift during ephemeral creation. Mitigation: use plan-only preflight and remote state isolation; module tags resources for safe teardown
Risk: Latency spike due to additional routing. Mitigation: limit siphon ratio to 2% and set autoscaling buffer for ephemeral control-plane replicas
